subject.title: fix(memory-core): honor private-network settings for OpenAI-compatible embeddings

question: Should OpenAI-compatible memory embedding fetches inherit `models.providers.<id>.request.allowPrivateNetwork`, including explicit `false` disabling exact-host trust, as the canonical fix for the linked private-endpoint issue?
rationale: The code path is small and appears correct, but the remaining choice changes an SSRF/private-network trust boundary and upgrade behavior for configured providers.

options.title: Accept Provider-Policy Inheritance
options.body: Merge this approach after maintainer/security acceptance, keeping provider `request.allowPrivateNetwork` as the single trust surface for configured memory embeddings.

options.title: Require Memory-Specific Trust Boundary
options.body: Ask for a rework if memory embeddings need a separate explicit policy instead of inheriting provider transport trust.

options.title: Reject Private-Network Embedding Opt-In
options.body: Close or pause the PR if maintainers do not want private/internal OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoints supported directly.

recommendation.title: Accept Provider-Policy Inheritance
recommendation.body: Merge this approach after maintainer/security acceptance, keeping provider `request.allowPrivateNetwork` as the single trust surface for configured memory embeddings.

likelyOwner.reason: They are tied to the merged memory bridge and provider architecture as both feature author and merger, making them the best available routing owner for this boundary choice.
